records.title: The Database Agent preflight reports PASS on a database with every migration unapplied

current_evidence.verification_scope: The Database Agent gate returned PASS over its own failing fields. records.title: Prisma migrate deploy cannot acquire its advisory lock through Neon pooled endpoint

current_evidence.verification_scope: Render deploy log of 2026-08-20 shows prisma migrate deploy failing P1002 after 10s on SELECT pg_advisory_lock(72707369), with the datasource resolved to Neon's -pooler host. prisma.config.ts:12-13 supplies one url from env('DATABASE_URL') for every Prisma CLI call and schema.prisma:11-13 declares no directUrl, so migrations inherit the runtime pooled connection. Session-scoped advisory locks cannot be held across PgBouncer transaction pooling, so the step cannot succeed at any timeout. Production stayed up on the prior revision; the release chain after the migration step did not run.

records.title: package-lock.json cannot be regenerated - npm overrides are silently ignored

current_evidence.verification_scope: Found while attempting the @mapbox/node-pre-gyp override for ITEM-0048. npm reads the overrides key - npm pkg get overrides returns it - and resolves as though it were absent, leaving no overrides key under packages[""] in the lockfile. Seven routes to a fresh resolution were tried; six were npm reusing a tree it considered satisfying, and the seventh, rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json followed by npm install --package-lock-only, failed with ERESOLVE on a @tiptap peer conflict in apps/admin. apps/admin pins the @tiptap family at 3.29.2 while @tiptap/extension-floating-menu, an optional peer of @tiptap/react, floats to 3.30.2 and demands @tiptap/core@3.30.2. The committed lockfile predates the conflict so npm ci succeeds and nothing has noticed. The override mechanism itself was verified working in an isolated scratch project on the first attempt.

records.title: Admin sign-out does not revoke the platform session when the refresh cookie has expired

current_evidence.verification_scope: AuthService.logout keyed revocation on the refresh token alone and read it only from the cookie, so a sign-out arriving after the refresh cookie's TTL elapsed — the ordinary case, and the exact flow BUG-0009 was raised about — cleared the browser and left the PlatformRefreshToken live for up to seven days. The fix revokes by the forwarded session cookie, filtered on { sessionId, appClientId, revokedAt: null }, using updateMany so a token rotated between a read and a write cannot survive the sign-out. Verification is REG-221: six DB-backed tests over real HTTP against a booted AppModule, covering the platform client and the tenant client, a session id belonging to nobody, and a session id belonging to a different client. Mutation-proven twice — removing the revocation call fails both primary tests, and removing appClientId from the filter fails the scope test. That second probe matters: the scope test's first version signed out as web with an admin session id and could not fail, because the two clients use different tables.

records.title: Exchange rate resolution ignored the effective date it was given

current_evidence.verification_scope: resolveExchangeRate took an effectiveDate and never queried it: all three lookups ordered by updatedAt and returned the newest row, so asking for the rate as of a date returned today's. ExchangeRateSnapshot is effective-dated by design and none of it was used. convertMoney forwards its caller's date, so a caller who supplied the right date still got the wrong number. Fixed by filtering every lookup on { effectiveDate: lte, effectiveEndDate null or gte } and ordering by effectiveDate descending first, so a later window covering the same moment is treated as the correction. Verification is REG-223: seven tests walking a real three-window history, asserting the returned rate AND the where clause, because a stub returns whatever row it holds regardless of the filter. Mutation-proven — replacing the filter with {} fails five of seven. Not reachable in production today: convertMoney has no callers, so this was a trap set for the first one rather than a wrong number already paid.

records.title: PATCH my-preferences never used its DTO so the body was unvalidated

current_evidence.verification_scope: UpdateMyPreferencesDto existed with IsString, MaxLength and Matches rules on all four fields and was never referenced; the handler took Record<string, unknown>, which gives the global ValidationPipe no metadata, so PATCH /settings/my-preferences accepted any body. normalizePreferences is an allow-list of four keys so this was never mass assignment: the exposure was the values, with unbounded strings persisted as sent and an invalid timezone reaching Intl.DateTimeFormat and surfacing as a 500 where 400 is the answer. Fixed by using the DTO as the parameter type and moving the class above the controller, because design:paramtypes is evaluated at class definition and a DTO below it sits in a temporal dead zone. Verification is REG-224: seven tests, the load-bearing one reading design:paramtypes to assert the parameter type itself, since a DTO's rules can be perfect and never run.

records.title: Customer emails link to the vercel.app host, and API_BASE_URL is plain HTTP

current_evidence.verification_scope: Two production environment variables on the Render service are wrong and the first is customer-facing. WEB_APP_URL is https://diji-people-web.vercel.app, so every activation, invitation, password-reset and sign-in link the API mails to a tenant sends them to the Vercel deployment host rather than app.dijipeople.com or their own workspace subdomain. API_BASE_URL is http://api.dijipeople.com/api while API_ORIGIN beside it is correctly https, and getApiBaseUrl prefers API_BASE_URL so the insecure value wins. The per-tenant subdomain rewrite in tenant-url.config.ts fires only when WEB_APP_PROD_ROOT_DOMAIN or NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_ROOT_DOMAIN is set, and neither is; TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN is set but is read by the hostname issuer, not the URL builder. Neither is a code defect and both are dashboard values, so the fix is a production environment write requiring the user's approval. Verification is that a tenant activation URL lands on the customer domain and /api/health reports an https apiBaseUrl, plus a test asserting the production shape - tenant-url.config.spec.ts currently encodes the misconfiguration as expected, which is why nothing flagged it.

dependencies.note: Needs approval to write four production environment variables on Render.

records.title: render.yaml is not what production runs, so no seed or legal publication has ever executed

current_evidence.verification_scope: The live Render service was configured by hand and did not match render.yaml: no preDeployCommand at all, with npx prisma migrate deploy bolted onto buildCommand instead. Migrations therefore applied and deploys looked correct, which is exactly why nobody noticed that seed:config, seed:verify, seed:admin, seed:legal and legal:publish had never executed on production. The consequence was not theoretical - the subscribe wizard requires agreements carrying a published version, so with none published it required none and no purchase could record consent. Verification is three-part: the live service configuration matches render.yaml, GET /api/public/legal returns the published documents, and a check fails when the file and the service disagree. The third part is the regression; without it this recurs the next time somebody edits the dashboard. Related and separate: publishing was attempted on 2026-08-22 and published ten documents whose own text declared them unreviewed drafts, which is why REG-230 now refuses any document that declares itself a draft.

records.title: Qatar market resolves to GCC because its country row is never repaired, so Doha visitors are quoted USD

current_evidence.verification_scope: MarketCountry.countryCode is unique globally, so GCC holding 'QA' made the Qatar market's own country row impossible to create. The seed caught that unique violation as benign and then skipped the market forever after, and the repair migration is guarded on the market existing while running before the seed that creates it. Production served a LAUNCHED, published, QAR-priced Qatar market that resolved for nobody, so every Doha visitor fell through to GCC at USD with no purchasable offer. Confirmed live against /api/public/commercial-config on 2026-08-22 at API commit 35f263c. Code fix is committed and unit-tested; the live data repair needs `npm run seed:commercial` run once against production, which is not in the release chain and is the owner's call because the same seed also reconciles plan prices.

records.title: Checkout quotes the alphabetically first plan price currency instead of the visitor market currency

The home page separately read /public/plans while /plans read commercial config, so the three surfaces could not agree by construction. records.title: Editing a plan price always fails with property syncToStripe should not exist

records.title: No end-to-end payment to provisioned tenant run against Stripe test mode

current_evidence.verification_scope: BUG-0077, BUG-0078 and BUG-0281 each cover their own half of the self-service purchase and each carries the same residual gap: nothing has driven a real payment through to a provisioned tenant. subscription-order.e2e-spec.ts proves the order and customer exist before payment; emitted-events-have-consumers.invariant.spec.ts proves PROVISIONING_REQUESTED has a registered consumer; checkout-customer-record.spec.ts proves the commercial and attribution columns are written. What no test does is let Stripe say paid and watch what follows, which crosses a webhook, the outbox, a provisioning run and the tenant control plane. The invariant that caught BUG-0078 is a source-level check: it proves a consumer is registered, not that the chain completes. Verification means Stripe test mode with webhook forwarding, driven from the database-e2e job, following a partner referral link through checkout with a test card and asserting the tenant exists, is reachable, and carries the partner attribution. A fabricated webhook payload posted directly is explicitly not sufficient: it exercises the handler, which is already covered, and skips the signature verification and delivery semantics that are the untested part.

records.title: Activation does not gate on a workspace having any module enabled

current_evidence.verification_scope: changeStatus refuses activation for two reasons its own comments explain — a workspace nobody can administer, and one nobody can reach — by filtering readiness down to ['workspace-slug', 'workspace-domain', 'workspace-routing'] plus the owner count. Readiness names a third way a workspace can be live and useless, 'No module is enabled, so the workspace has nothing a user can open', marks it BLOCKER, and the gate does not check it. A tenant therefore reaches ACTIVE, its owner signs in successfully, and lands somewhere empty. Found while closing ITEM-0004; visible there because that suite's fixture plan entitles no modules, whereas an ordinary provisioning run entitles something and the blocker never appears. Raised as PRODUCT_DECISION rather than a bug because extending an activation gate could block legitimate activations where modules are enabled afterwards, and refusing an operator's action is not a change to make on an agent's judgement. Verification is the assertion in tenant-activation.e2e-spec.ts that pins today's behaviour: if the gate is extended, that test fails and names this record, so the decision cannot be silently lost.
